ST-059.title: We fix furnace problems, from no heat to new noises.
ST-059.summary: Tell us what changed. MGI Heating and Air can check the cause and explain the repair before you choose the work.
ST-059.label: Request furnace repair
ST-059.close: Tell us what your furnace is doing
ST-059.closeBody: Start with when the heat changed and what you notice now. You can request a repair visit without choosing a part or agreeing to replacement.
ST-059.safety: Gas smell? Leave. From a safe place, call 911 and your gas utility. Do not use switches or try to relight the furnace. Suspected carbon monoxide? Get outside to fresh air and call 911. Smoke or immediate danger? Leave and call 911 from a safe place.
faqs: Can a repair be finished on the first visit?
That depends on the fault and whether the needed parts are available. If a part must be ordered, ask about the next step and any added cost.
Does furnace age mean replacement?
No. Condition, past repairs, available parts, and the heat your home needs matter too. Compare what each choice would fix before deciding.
What should I know about the diagnostic charge?
Get the visit charge, what it covers, and any credit toward the repair clear before arranging the visit. The repair price is a separate detail.
What if the same problem returns?
Keep the findings and repair record. Refer to the written parts and labor terms, and contact the office with the original concern and what changed.

ST-060.title: We help you choose and install a new furnace.
ST-060.summary: MGI Heating and Air helps you compare repair with replacement and plan a new furnace installation. Start with your home, the findings, and the full project.
ST-060.label: Request a replacement assessment
ST-060.closeBody: Bring your concerns, past repairs, and any quotes you want to compare. A consultation request starts the conversation. It does not authorize a purchase.
ST-060.safety: If you smell gas, leave the area. From a safe place, call 911 and your gas utility. Do not use switches or try to relight the furnace. If you suspect carbon monoxide, get outside to fresh air and call 911. For smoke or other immediate danger, leave the area and call 911 from a safe place.
faqs: How is the furnace size chosen?
The choice should fit the heat the home needs, not just match the old furnace. Ask what the sizing recommendation is based on and how the proposed model fits those needs.
What should the estimate include?
Equipment and installation work, what stays, what is removed, and any separate trade or permit responsibility. Make sure added work and checks at the finish are clear.
How long will installation take?
The work in your home sets the timeline. Get a project-specific plan, including time without heat and any work that must happen first.
What warranty applies?
Equipment and labor coverage can have different terms. Read the written coverage, registration duties, exclusions, and contact route before choosing.
Will a higher efficiency rating lower my bill?
The rating alone does not establish a lower bill. Fuel price, home heat loss, weather, and use also affect the cost. A useful estimate names its assumptions.

ST-063.title: We help you stay on top of furnace care.
ST-063.summary: MGI Heating and Air provides furnace maintenance. Plan a care visit with the checks, price, and any separate work clear before you agree.
ST-063.label: Request furnace maintenance
ST-063.close: Plan the care your furnace needs
ST-063.closeBody: Share the furnace model or past service record if you have it. You can start without those details. A maintenance request does not enroll you in a membership.
ST-063.safety: If you smell gas, leave the area. From a safe place, call 911 and your gas utility. Do not use switches or try to relight the furnace. If you suspect carbon monoxide, get outside to fresh air and call 911. For smoke or other immediate danger, leave the area and call 911 from a safe place.
faqs: How often should my furnace be checked?
ENERGY STAR recommends annual preseason heating checkups. The furnace's instructions and a qualified assessment guide care for your exact equipment.
Is a new filter included?
Filter type and supply are part of the visit terms. Check whether a filter is supplied or charged separately. Follow the furnace's instructions for the right filter.
What if a problem is found?
Get the finding, its meaning, and the recommended next step clear. A care visit and a repair are separate decisions; understand any added charge before approving work.
Should I wait for maintenance if the heat stops?

No heat is a repair concern. Use the repair path and describe what stopped. If you smell gas, leave and call 911 and your gas utility from a safe place. If you suspect carbon monoxide, get outside to fresh air and call 911. For other immediate danger, leave and call 911 from a safe place.

sections.heading: What a professional check can cover
sections.body: ENERGY STAR describes common heating checks. They explain the kind of work involved; the tasks included in your MGI visit depend on the agreed visit terms.
rows: Controls
Check whether the thermostat and controls start, run, and stop the heat as intended.
Electrical parts
Check connections and the power supplied to the motor. These are professional checks, not homeowner tasks.
Fuel and heat
Check gas connections, gas pressure, the burner, and the heat exchanger, the part that transfers heat to the air. These checks need a qualified person.
